messages.content: Explain how an airplane wing generates lift. Answer in two to four sentences of plain prose.

message.content: An airplane wing generates lift by deflecting air downward as it moves through the air; by Newton's third law, pushing air down produces an equal upward reaction force on the wing. The wing's shape and its angle of attack (tilt relative to the oncoming air) cause the airflow to curve and accelerate over the upper surface, creating lower pressure above the wing than below it. This pressure difference, integrated across the wing's area, is what we measure as lift. Both the Newtonian "air deflection" view and the pressure-difference view describe the same physical phenomenon from different perspectives.
